title: An unauthenticated client could fill the SSO pending-sign-in table and block sign-ins
description:
The SSO sign-ins under way are bounded by a global cap of 10000 entries kept for 10 minutes, and the per-source limit is coarse (per exact IP), so an IPv6 /64 or about 90 IPv4 addresses could fill the table with unfinished sign-ins. Every SSO sign-in then answered "too many sign-ins under way" for up to 10 minutes. Password sign-in was unaffected.

**Affected**: a Controller with SSO enabled, reachable by an unauthenticated client.

**Fix**: when the table is full, the oldest sign-in under way is evicted and the new one is kept, so a flood only churns its own entries instead of blocking everyone's for the table's lifetime.

**Besides updating**: nothing.
